result.query: Photoshop with generative AI fill for raw photos

picks.name: GIMP
picks.why: GIMP covers 56% of your must-haves, runs on your platform, open source (GPL-3.0-or-later). A free option for what you would use Adobe Photoshop for.

gaps.label: RAW photo editing
gaps.workaround: Open RAW files through darktable or RawTherapee, which GIMP hands off to automatically.

gaps.label: Generative AI fill
gaps.workaround: Run an open model locally, e.g. the GIMP Stable Diffusion plug-ins, and check each model's license.

gaps.label: Open and save PSD files
gaps.workaround: GIMP opens layered PSDs; adjustment layers and smart objects are flattened.

gaps.label: Content-aware fill / healing
gaps.workaround: Use the Heal tool or the Resynthesizer plug-in (GPL).

buildPlan.reason: The best free pick, GIMP, covers only 56% of your must-haves (the bar is 70%).
buildPlan.concept: An original creative tool that helps with: RAW photo editing, Generative AI fill. It gets the same job done in its own way, under its own name.
suggestedFoundation: Extend GIMP (GPL-3.0-or-later) through its plug-in or scripting system if it has one, so you only build the missing parts.
Pick permissively licensed libraries (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) or copyleft ones (GPL, LGPL, MPL) whose terms you are happy to follow; check each id on the SPDX license list.
Find assets on openly licensed sources such as OpenGameArt or Wikimedia Commons, and record each license.
steps: Write a one-page brief in your own words: who it is for, the jobs it does, and the vibe it should have.
List the smallest set of features that makes it useful, starting with the gaps above.
Choose the base (an existing open-source project or libraries) and confirm every license is compatible with yours.
Build a rough prototype of one gap and try it with a few real users.
Choose an open-source license for your project, add LICENSE and CREDITS files, and publish the code.
cleanRoomRules: Describe the job to be done in your own words; never copy the paid product's code, UI layouts, icons, art, sounds or text.
Do not decompile, disassemble or reverse engineer the paid product, and do not read its leaked source.
Use your own name and branding; do not use the paid product's trademarks, logos or characters.
Build only on components whose licenses allow it, keep their license files, and credit them in a NOTICE or CREDITS file.
Use openly licensed assets (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA) and record the author and license of each one.
Read and match file formats only from public specifications or your own test files.
